rationale: Both candidates independently rediscover the real, still-live bug that the model-specific 0.17 default never reaches the runtime because the engine injects 0.2 before TeaCacheConfig sees it — this is the closest match to the ground-truth's headline threshold concern, and both also flag that the E2E smoke test can't prove a cache hit occurred, echoing the reviewer's own validation note. Y is organized more like a professional review (blocking/should-fix/minor/verified-correct), adds several additional well-grounded findings (memory retention of two full packed tensors, wasted RoPE computation on cached steps, a drive-by shared-helper change that silently altered an unrelated FP8 test, and a design-consistency note on hard-fail vs. warn-and-disable) without overclaiming. X's polynomial-floor analysis is sharp but a couple of its items (the Cache-DiT table question, the open-ended CI gate question) are speculative rather than resolved findings, slightly denting precision relative to Y's more consistently grounded and actionable list.
